review.publication: Local only. No commit, push or deployment.
review.scope: Visible light, lighting states, perceived brightness and colour lightness; photometric quantities, units, measurements and meters; pale colours misplaced under the lighting process.
review.attribution: Reviewed adaptations of Open English WordNet 2025 by the Open English WordNet Team, derived from Princeton WordNet; CC BY 4.0 and Princeton notices remain in docs/quality/2026-10-09-q11.md#sources-and-reuse. CIE, BIPM and Gramota support selected corrections. Source definitions are paraphrased, not copied; Russian labels and graph mappings are editorial adaptations.
review.context_policy: All additions use U1 and unspecified strength. Illumination state, lighting activity, radiation, visual perception and physical quantity are distinct meanings. A photometric value depends on the specified geometry and spectral weighting. No observer-independent identity between brightness and luminance is asserted.

sense_decisions.scope: The ambient lighting condition of an environment. Distinct from the action of illuminating it, a photometric illuminance value and the meteorological visibility distance. Correct the vague degree-of-visibility wording.
The state in which an environment is lit, contrasted with darkness in that environment. Not visible radiation as a physical phenomenon.
A physical light quantity evaluated with a specified visual-response weighting. Distinguish it from the corresponding unweighted radiometric quantity and from an individual visual sensation.
The photometrically weighted flow rate of radiant energy. It is measured in lumens; do not import a raw radiant-power genus or a per-area definition.
Directional luminous flux per solid angle, measured in candelas. Not generic perceived brightness or electric current.
Incident luminous flux per surface area, measured in lux. It is not a kind of luminance, and the process word illumination is not imported as its unqualified synonym.

The directional light quantity using luminous intensity and projected surface area. Measured in candelas per square metre; exclude the source synset's mixed perceptual brightness and generic light synonyms.
A unit for luminous flux, not luminous flux per area. Correct the dictionary gloss.
A unit for the illuminance quantity, distinct from lighting activity.
A unit for physical luminance, not an individual brightness sensation.
The SI luminous-flux unit. Exclude the anatomical cavity sense.
The SI illuminance unit. Exclude luxury-related trade labels and the general lighting state.

sense_decisions.alignment: explicit name for the nit unit sense
sense_decisions.scope: The SI luminance unit. Use the explicit unit name rather than the ambiguous bare nit synonym.
The existing luminous-intensity unit family already has the correct unit genus.
Candela is already present under luminous-intensity unit; retain its direct genus and all prior conditions.
Measuring photometric quantities. Select the measurement activity, not the discipline or a single instrument reading.
Measurement of the selected photometric quantity, with suitable geometry and response weighting.
Measurement of the selected photometric quantity, with suitable geometry and response weighting.
Measurement of the selected photometric quantity, with suitable geometry and response weighting.
Measurement of the selected photometric quantity, with suitable geometry and response weighting.
An instrument for photometric measurement. Do not require every photometer to compare only source intensity or to be a photographic exposure meter.
A photometer intended to measure illuminance.
A photometer intended to measure luminance.
The visual attribute by which an area seems more or less bright. Keep the perceptual meaning separate from a luminance measurement and from intelligence.
Relative visual brightness judged against a similarly lit white or highly transmitting reference. Not the amount of incident light and not low weight.
Natural visible light available during the day. Distinct from the daytime interval already represented in the database.
The visible-light sense of light from the Sun. Do not import the Sun object or identify this with all solar radiation.
Visible light reaching the environment from the illuminated Moon, by reflection. Not a Moon object or a claim that the Moon generates its own visible radiation.
This pale-grey record duplicates existing light-grey 4953; defer to a reviewed leaf merge, not a false subtype link.
The radiation verb-derived record needs a separate duplicate/sense review against existing emission process 258.
Lighting remains a physical process; its hair, skin, enlightened and pale-grey descendants need further sense review.
Retain shadow phenomenon and its existing dependency on light. Removing its unqualified contrary relation does not make it a kind of darkness.

review.limits: No numerical light levels, exposure or health guidance, efficacy rankings, spectral-response algorithms, exact colour coordinates or mandatory lamp components. Unit conversions remain explanatory scope, not graph arithmetic. Lamp and luminaire types, mixed hair/skin/enlightened lighting descendants, the pale-grey duplicate and radiation-process duplicates remain queued. No application test suites.

exclusion_review.decision: Darkness is reparented to lighting state; its state/radiation opposition is replaced by a state/state contrary. The unqualified light/shadow opposition is removed. No new conflicting pair or witness is accepted.

review.collision_decision: No exact normalized cross-language collision is accepted. Existing light, darkness, colours, units and instrument/measurement anchors are reused. A substring hit for lux in luxurious is not an exact collision.

refreshed_comparison.caveat: Normalized spelling candidates are not verified identities or missing-concept counts.
